description:
Creates, lists, prints, copies, deletes and renders notes. Each note is identified by its stem: the filename without .md, e.g. 2026-09-10-14-30-00.

Subcommands:
  new --type TYPE --topic TOPIC --thread THREAD [--person P] [--counterparty C] [--location L] — create a note and print its path
  list [FILTER] [--json] — list notes oldest first, showing stem, date, type, threads and topic
  cat STEM — print a note
  last — print the path of the newest note
  copy STEM — copy a note to a new timestamp; ' COPY' is appended to its topic
  delete STEM -y — permanently delete a note
  pdf STEM [--out DIR] — render the note to markdown and PDF, with callouts and an action table
  minutes STEM [--out DIR] — render meeting minutes: agreements, resolutions and action items
  agenda STEM [--out DIR] — render a meeting agenda: the note with its outcome sections emptied

Flags:
  new:
    --type          required. One of: Meeting, Correspondence, Workshop, Report, Log, Research, Recipe
    --topic TEXT    required. What the note is about.
    --thread T      required; repeatable. Thread name, 'Kind/Name' or wikilink.
    --person NAME   Meeting and Correspondence only; repeatable. Linked when people/NAME.md exists.
    --counterparty  Meeting only. The other party.
    --location      Meeting only. Where the meeting was held.
  list:
    FILTER  case-insensitive text matched against any column
    --json  JSON output
  delete:
    -y, --yes  required to confirm the delete
  pdf, minutes, agenda:
    --out DIR  output directory. Default: the user's Downloads folder. Writes STEM.md and STEM.md.pdf, then prints both paths.

Examples:
  ["new", "--type", "Meeting", "--topic", "Budget review", "--thread", "Projects/SGB", "--person", "Jane Doe", "--location", "Office"]
  ["list", "budget"]
  ["cat", "2026-09-10-14-30-00"]
  ["delete", "2026-09-10-14-30-00", "-y"]

Notes:
  Every subcommand except new first runs task ingest, which rewrites ACTION: lines in notes and logs in place.
  delete is permanent. Without -y it does not delete.
  new queues a REF in the buffer. It reaches the thread's log on the next `buffer flush`.
  pdf, minutes and agenda need pandoc and a LaTeX engine. If the render fails, the command exits 1.
  Exit code 1 also means: a bad or unknown stem, an empty topic, or a Meeting/Correspondence-only flag used on another note type.
